title: Pseudo-coherence on projective space detected by finitely many derived twists
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $N\geq0$. Put $P=\operatorname{Proj}(R[x_0,\ldots,x_N])$, with twists $\mathcal O_P(d)$ as in [def-pc-projective-space-twist]. Let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_P)$ [def-pc-derived-category], meaning an object of the derived category of $\mathcal O_P$-modules whose cohomology sheaves are quasi-coherent. Suppose that, for each $d=0,1,\ldots,N$, the derived global-section complex [def-pc-global-derived-rhom] $R\Gamma(P,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_P}\mathcal O_P(d))\in D(R)$ is pseudo-coherent [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. Here the derived tensor is that of [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Then $K$ is pseudo-coherent on $P$ [def-pur-pseudo-coherent-complex].

proof.text: Put $T=\bigoplus_{i=0}^N\mathcal O_P(-i)$ and $B=\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O_P}(T)$. The projective-space tilting equivalence supplies $M\in D(\operatorname{Mod}\!\text{-}B)$ with $M\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}T\simeq K$ and $\operatorname{Res}_R M\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_P(T,K)$ in $D(R)$. This uses the unbounded equivalence, so imposes no preliminary boundedness condition on $K$.

The bundle $T$ is perfect: on every standard open $U_j=D_+(x_j)$ it is the finite free module with basis the specified bases of the $N+1$ twists, placed in degree zero. Its dual is $T^\vee=\bigoplus_{d=0}^N\mathcal O_P(d)$: the pairing on the $d$th summand multiplies the local twist bases to $1$, and their inverse transition factors cancel. Perfect duality and the definition of global derived Hom give $$R\operatorname{Hom}_P(T,K)\simeq R\Gamma(P,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}T^\vee)\simeq\bigoplus_{d=0}^N R\Gamma(P,K\otimes^{\mathbf L}\mathcal O_P(d)).$$ The second isomorphism uses finite biproducts: the tensor and global-section functors are additive, their finite-sum inclusions and projections retain the identities $p_di_e=\delta_{de}$ and $\sum_di_dp_d=1$ after derivation (finite sums of resolving complexes remain resolving).

For each of these $N+1$ summands choose a bounded-above finite-free $R$-complex representing it, using the assumed pseudo-coherence. Their finite termwise direct sum is again finite free in each degree, is zero above the maximum of their finitely many upper bounds, and represents the displayed biproduct: cohomology commutes with finite direct sums. Thus the underlying object $\operatorname{Res}_R M$ is pseudo-coherent.

In the matrix description of $B$, each block $S_{j-i}$ is finite free over $R$ on the monomials of fixed degree $j-i$ in $N+1$ variables. There are only finitely many such monomials and finitely many blocks. Hence $B$ is finite free over $R$, including when $N=0$. Apply the finite-free algebra resolution lemma to $M$ and its pseudo-coherent underlying $R$-complex. Obtain a bounded-above complex $F^\bullet$ of finite free right $B$-modules representing $M$.

Use the bounded-above projective-complex computation lemma for $V(L)=L\otimes_B T$ (sheaf tensor as in the tilting node). Its total left derived functor exists on all objects by that node. The functor is additive and right exact, since balanced tensor is given by a cokernel and sheafification is exact. Right $B$-modules have enough projectives by the free module on their underlying set; a free module is projective because maps from its basis lift across a surjection. Therefore the bounded-above finite-free complex $F^\bullet$ computes $LV(M)$, and $$K\simeq Q(F^\bullet\otimes_B T).$$ If $F^i\simeq B^{r_i}$, its tensor with $T$ is $T^{\oplus r_i}$, by $(b_a)_a\otimes t\mapsto(b_at)_a$. On every $U_j$ this is free of rank $(N+1)r_i$; the resulting complex has the same upper bound as $F^\bullet$. Thus $K$ has on these opens a bounded-above finite-free representative, exactly the definition of pseudo-coherence on $P$.
